reviewed_by: Claude review of device lookup and language-server diagnostics
reason: _device_for_token in api.py scanned the first 1,000 PairedDeviceSession rows (list_entities orders oldest first) for the presented cookie's token hash, so once a Core had recorded that many pairings over its lifetime every newer device got 401 on every request and was missing from the device list. NebulaStore.find_entity now looks the hash up in SQL; the revocation and expiry checks are unchanged. Separately, every record_caught_exception call in language_server.py named the feature 'language_server', which diagnostics._normalize_feature rejects because it is not in FEATURE_FILES; with a diagnostics manager configured (production, not pytest) the except blocks themselves raised, turning a ruff timeout into a JSON-RPC error for formatting, suppressing published diagnostics, and closing the LSP socket with 1011 from the catch-all handler. The calls now use the registered 'workspace' feature. test_api gains a request authenticated by a device paired after 1,000 older sessions (401 on main, 200 now); the new test_language_server_diagnostics asserts every feature named in language_server.py is registered (fails on main); test_language_server covers the handler paths that record those diagnostics.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (matched through api.py and storage.py) is the real-Core journey suite and pairs at most one device; the Python tests create the thousand sessions directly and exercise the language-server handlers in process. No full suites.
